A_real_sweep.note: classical window G>-1/4 (two real roots); quantum window G<-1/4 (conjugate phase pair, common modulus sqrt(-G)); |root|=1 exactly at G=-1.

B_monodromy.note: The direction of approach to -1/4 is not decoration: the branch point carries a Z2 monodromy. Circle round it once, the two roots trade places. Same Z2 that survived the Galois twist in circle-six H^3. The invariant holds; the LABELS braid.

C_mandelbrot_bridge.note: classical stability (attracting fixed pt) = interior of main cardioid; the branch point is PARABOLIC dynamics (multiplier exactly 1). The most quantum gap (G=-1, roots on unit circle) lies OUTSIDE the set: pure phase never settles. Classical=inside, quantum=escape, the cusp is the door.

D_recursion.note: The nilpotent solution Golden.lean proves unique to -1/4 is not exotic: in the time domain it is the secular term n·(1/2)^n — the sound of two modes becoming one. Criticality IS the dual number.

E_gap_set_law: (x+ - x-)^2 = 1 + 4G for every G: THE GAP BETWEEN THE ROOTS SATISFIES ITS OWN EQUATION, one level up. gamma^2 = 1 + 4G  — the gap of the gap is affine in the gap.

F1_finite_fields.golden_exists_mod_p_iff: 5 is a QR mod p  <=>  p = +-1 mod 5
F1_finite_fields.p5_special: x^2=x+1 has the DOUBLE root 3 mod 5 — the finite-field shadow of the branch point: 1+4G = 5 = 0 mod 5. In F_5 the golden gap IS the collision. -1/4 mod 5 = 1. The branch point and the golden gap are THE SAME RESIDUE in F_5.

F2_char2.gap_set_collapse: in F_2:  +1 = -1  and  i = 1  (since x^2=-1 => x=1). All four gaps {+1,-1,+i,-i} become ONE gap. The golden ratio in characteristic 2 IS the cube root of unity. phi*psi=-1 and phi*psi=+1 stop being different claims.
F2_char2.artin_schreier: completing the square needs 1/2; char 2 replaces x^2-x=G (Artin-Schreier) — already in circle-six GAP/lean/ArtinSchreier.lean.

F3_padic.Q5: v_5(sqrt5)=1/2 not an integer: phi needs the RAMIFIED extension Q_5(sqrt5). The golden ratio sits exactly on a ramification point of the 5-adic world — the same prime that indexes it in R (sqrt5), again refusing to be ordinary.

F4_quaternions.solution_set: a 2-SPHERE: x = 1/2 + (sqrt(-(1+4G))/2)·u for EVERY imaginary unit u
F4_quaternions.note: Same equation, bigger algebra: the two quantum roots inflate into a continuum. C chooses an axis (±i); H refuses to choose. The "two roots" were never two THINGS — they were two labels on one sphere, visible only after an axis is picked. Relational lens vindicated by dimension count: classical 0-sphere (2 pts) -> complex 0-sphere embedded with phase -> quaternionic 2-sphere.

G_tower.meaning_of_2: x^2=x+2 has roots {2,-1}: the first INTEGER pair past golden. The tower of gaps eats itself and lands on the simplest split: 2 and -1. Self-reference terminates in integers.

I_sound.script: G sweeps 1 -> -1 over 12s. Start: the golden chord (pitch ratio phi^2 = phi+1, the only interval equal to itself plus an octave-of-itself). At G=-1/4 (t=7.5s) the two voices FUSE into unison at 110 Hz — you can hear the branch point as the death of harmony into a single line. For G<-1/4 both moduli are sqrt(-G): ONE pitch rising, and the difference between the roots survives only as stereo phase — audible as space, not as tone. Classical = interval. Quantum = placement.

ONE_SENTENCE: The gap is not the flaw in the equation; it is the coordinate the whole family of solutions breathes through, and “kinds of number” — real, imaginary, nilpotent, finite, spherical — are just the shapes the same two roots take when you walk up to −1/4 from different directions.
